summary: Feed s126_double is degraded: IDS is overloaded by 1.47 Gbps microbursts vs 1 Gbps port (147% capacity, 9 intervals) and required VLANs 10,20 are completely missing (100% untagged), causing packet loss and VLAN blind spots.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or SPAN/TAP is stripping 802.1Q tags before delivery - 100% of packets arrived untagged so required VLANs 10 and 20 are not seen. Typically caused by broker egress port in access/untag mode or SPAN stripping tags.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot identify or apply VLAN-aware detection for VLANs 10 and 20; all traffic appears as untagged, creating complete blind spot for those segments and missed intrusions.

recommended_fix.why: Restore and preserve 802.1Q tags end-to-end through TAP/SPAN and packet broker so IDS receives VLAN 10,20 correctly for segmentation and detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Aggregate/burst throughput exceeds IDS ingress capacity: peaks of 1.47 Gbps in 1ms bursts vs 1 Gbps port (147% utilization, 9 overloaded intervals, threshold 80%). Broker is sending more than single tool port can handle.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS will drop packets at ingress during bursts, breaking its needs_full_payload and needs_both_directions requirements; results in missed signatures, truncated flows, and attacker evasion.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 2+ IDS ports/instances via packet broker flow-based load balancing to keep per-port utilization below 80% and eliminate burst drops while preserving full payload and bidirectional flows.
